reasons: The lake identity record identifies the case as United States v. Osage, decided by the U.S. Court of Appeals, 10th Circuit on 2000-12-15.
The lake citations list official cite 235 F.3d 518, parallel cite 2000 Colo. J. C.A.R. 6671, and vendor-neutral cites 2000 U.S. App. LEXIS 32020 and 2000 WL 1842404.
The opinion is a consent-search scope case: it states that when officers rely on consent for a warrantless search, the scope of consent determines the permissible scope of the search.

The opinion limits the general consent/container rule by holding that consent did not permit destruction or complete uselessness of the container, supporting the home role Limiting on Consent Searches.

The stated holding is directly supported by the opinion's rule: before an officer may destroy or render completely useless an otherwise searchable container, the officer must obtain explicit authorization or have another lawful basis.

The opinion applies that rule to reverse denial of suppression because opening the sealed can exceeded the scope of consent, and the government disavowed reliance on suspicion, probable cause, or another ground.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: For maximum fidelity, mirror the opinion's wording: 'a container which would otherwise be within the scope of a permissive search.'
